title: permanent_mod3_reference faithful Rust port of paper Julia
description:
Implement `permanent_mod3_reference` as a faithful line-by-line port of the paper's published Julia algorithm; this is the in-tree baseline against which the headline 50× speedup is measured.

## Background

The reference paper publishes Julia source for `permanent_mod3` (Algorithm in §3 / Appendix A of arxiv:2407.20205v2). This issue ports it to Rust with no substantive algorithmic changes — only the minimum needed to compile in the project's `Fp<3>` field. The port is the in-tree perf baseline for criterion S1 (T9 must beat this by $\ge 50\times$ at $n=36$).

This is **not** the SIMD or bipedal-packed path (those are T9 and T12). It is the literal Rust counterpart to the published Julia, so the 50× claim has a defensible per-machine baseline that doesn't depend on Julia toolchain mood.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_mod3_reference(matrix: &[Fp<3>], n: usize) -> Fp<3>` exists.
- [ ] [hard] Implementation is a line-by-line port of the paper's Julia `permanent_mod3` listing, with comment markers calling out each port-section against the paper's pseudocode.
- [ ] [hard] Output bit-identical to `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (T7) on 1000 random matrices for each $n \in \{1, \ldots, 12\}$.
- [ ] [hard] No SIMD, no rayon, no bipedal-packing; this is the unoptimised reference.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes.
